reasons.docs/MEDICHAM-SPRINT-NOTES.md|117|data/t: HAND EDIT, 2026-08-13, ROADMAP #261. THE FIGURE DID NOT CHANGE AND NEITHER DID ITS DOCUMENT — the ARTIFACT it was coincidentally matching did. `docs/MEDICHAM-SPRINT-NOTES.md:5759` states a roster result from 2026-08-11 ("on abilities, FIRED-AND-BOARDS-MATCH 107 -> 117"); the nearest artifact its block cites is data/tags.json, and 117 appeared FOUR times in that file as a corpus usage count, so the citation check passed on a collision rather than on a citation. Regenerating data/tags.json for the thawsUser/thawsTarget split re-read those usage counts and 117 no longer occurs, which exposed a figure that has been untraceable since the day it was written. Measured, not assumed: OLD tags.json 4 occurrences of 117, NEW 0. It is a ROSTER number and belongs to data/roster.abilities.json; re-citing an earlier pass's measurement is that pass's job, not this one's, so it is recorded here rather than silently rewritten.
reasons.untraceable_by_doc|RESTORED 2026-08-15: THESE EIGHT COUNTS WERE PUT BACK BY HAND, and the reason is the only reason a ratchet may ever be written by hand: a run had corrupted them DOWNWARD, which is stricter than the truth and would have left the gate permanently red against a floor no correct run could meet. The corruption was self-reference — data/docs-currency-baseline.json is itself a .json under data/, so engine/docs_scan.js#allArtifactNumbers was reading the census own record of a figure as EVIDENCE FOR that figure. Recording the untraceable SET took docs/ABRA-whitepaper.md from 12 to 5 in one run; the same loop had been live through citation_mismatches, which has carried figure values since it was written. allArtifactNumbers now excludes this file (NOT_AN_ARTIFACT). The values restored are the ones this file held at 2026-08-15T03:11:13.624Z. SECOND RESTORE, SAME RUN: docs/ROLE-FAMILY.md had been laundered to zero by data/open-work.json and a green run then DROPPED it from this list entirely, so closing the loop made it read as a document that was never baselined. It is put back at the 2 it held at 03:11:13.624Z. The counts in this list are the pre-session truth and are NOT to be raised: docs/MEDICHAM-SPRINT-NOTES.md now measures 32 against a recorded 25 and docs/ABRA-whitepaper.md 12 against 11 — the first seven are a DISCOVERY (the register was masking them), the twelfth is a real REGRESSION whose cause is an expired numeric collision in an artifact rewritten tonight. ROADMAP #188 is the row about a ratchet with no regression-vs-discovery split; this is that row happening.

note_unversioned: These documents carry no version header, so nothing can say whether they are current. They are EXEMPT FROM RULE 1 ONLY - they are still scanned by the retracted-number rules. The list may only shrink: give a document a version header matching the CHANGELOG and it leaves this list and joins the figure scans.
note_archive: docs/archive/ files that do NOT declare a SUPERSEDED replacement. Grandfathering here only stops the SUPERSEDED-header rule failing; it grants NO exemption from the content scans, and the sixteen files archived on 2026-08-05 were deliberately left undeclared for exactly that reason. Moving a file into docs/archive/ must not convert a caught retracted figure into an uncaught one, so these carry a provenance header (what it claimed / when / what replaced it / what in it is retracted) and STAY in rules 1, 1b and 3b. Use the SUPERSEDED form only for a document whose content is wholly reproduced elsewhere. docs/archive/INDEX.md is GENERATED by build/build_archive_index.js and is the index over this directory, not an archived document.
note_known: What rule 3 found on 2026-08-05. Every entry is a REPORTED DEFECT, not an approval. The ratchet exists so the list cannot grow while these are worked through; it is not a statement that any of them is acceptable. Fixing a document retires its entry automatically on the next run.
